_note: Shipcast platform formats. Researched Nov 2026 from the platforms' published specs and common practice. safe = px from each edge the platform covers with its own buttons, captions or crops; keep text inside.

formats.label: Feed post
formats.why: 4:5 portrait takes the most space in the feed. The profile grid shows a centred 3:4 crop, so key content stays away from the top and bottom edges.
formats.vibe: Polished and visual. One bold idea per post, a short headline, the real product front and centre.
formats.caption: First line is the hook (it shows before 'more'). Then 2–4 short lines of value, one clear call to action, then hashtags on their own line.

formats.label: Carousel
formats.why: Carousels get swiped and saved. Slide 1 is the hook, the middle slides teach or show, the last slide sums up with the product name and a call to action. Instagram's dots sit at the bottom.
formats.vibe: Clear and useful: a mini guide or a feature walkthrough. Each slide one point, consistent layout across slides.
formats.caption: Hook line, one line on what the carousel shows, a call to action ('Save this', 'Swipe'), then hashtags.

formats.label: Reel
formats.why: Reels are full-screen vertical video. The top and the bottom fifth are covered by Instagram's buttons and caption; the right edge holds the like/comment column.
formats.vibe: Energetic and quick. Readable hook within the first second, one idea per beat, big on-screen text — it plays muted.
formats.caption: One punchy line, one line of value, a call to action, then hashtags.

formats.label: Video
formats.why: TikTok is vertical video first. Its buttons run down the right edge and its caption covers the bottom quarter.
formats.vibe: Native and playful. 'Watch this' energy, a hook in the first second, show the product doing something, captions on screen.
formats.caption: Short and casual, like a person talking. One line plus 3–5 hashtags.

formats.label: Photo carousel
formats.why: TikTok photo mode is a swipeable vertical slideshow with the same button and caption areas as video.
formats.vibe: Bold and simple. One big line per slide, the product in every frame.
formats.caption: Short and casual, 3–5 hashtags.

formats.label: Portrait image
formats.why: Portrait images take the most room in the LinkedIn feed on phones, where most people read it.
formats.vibe: Professional and specific: the problem, what was built, the result. Confident, no hype, no emoji walls.
formats.caption: A strong first line (shown before 'see more'), 3–6 short lines on the problem and what the product does, a question or call to action, then up to 3 hashtags.

formats.label: Square image
formats.why: Square looks the same on desktop and phone — good for announcements and screenshots.
formats.vibe: Professional and specific. Confident, no hype.
formats.caption: A strong first line, 3–6 short lines, a question or call to action, up to 3 hashtags.

formats.label: Video
formats.why: LinkedIn videos autoplay muted in a portrait-friendly feed, so the story must work through on-screen text alone.
formats.vibe: Calm and confident. Show the product step by step with clear captions, end on the product name.
formats.caption: A strong first line, 2–4 short lines, a call to action, up to 3 hashtags.
